title: 9 spooky things to do this Halloween in Louisiana's most haunted city
excerpt: Louisiana is home to plenty of ghost stories, but the spookiest city in the state is the best place to visit for Halloween, according to Southern Living.
content:
Oct. 20, 2026, 8:54 a.m. CT

The U.S. is full of spooky places to visit during Halloween, where places are filled with legends of the dead walking among the living.

While there are famous New England spots, like Sleepy Hollow, New York and Salem, Massachusetts, the South is also home to haunted destinations like Savannah, Georgia and New Orleans.

New Orleans is often said to be the most haunted city in the country, with tragic tales making up local folklore and haunting mysteries tied to the city's spiritual realm.

New Orleans on Halloween

Being one of the most haunted places, New Orleans comes alive during October for Halloween, with plenty of events, experiences and, of course, haunts taking place this time of year.

Halloween events in New Orleans

Here are some events that are taking place around Halloween in New Orleans that Southern Living recommends:

  • The Krewe of Boo Parade: An elaborate costume parade that will take place on Oct. 25 at 6:30 p.m., featuring 1,000 participating members and premiere, spooky floats.
  • Candlelight Halloween Classics by Orchestra: Hear orchestra renditions of classic Halloween tunes by flickering candlelight. The Ogden Museum of Art and The Sazerac House will both be participating locations this year.
  • Rocky Horror Picture Show at Mahalia Jackson Theater: See the cult classic "Rocky Horror Picture Show" at Mahalia Jackson Theater, emceed by Nell Campbell.
  • Queen’s Labyrinth Halloween Masquerade Ball: A masked, black-tie event filled with actors who create a fantasy land. Guests can grab a cocktail at the gate and step inside to encounter hidden bars and secret rendezvous. The theme changes annually and, each year, there is a Queen of Court.

Halloween experiences in New Orleans recommended by Southern Living

Here are some Halloween experiences South Living recommends taking part in this Halloween:

  • The Black Lagoon at Anna’s: The Black Lagoon at the award-winning cocktail dive bar, Anna's, is an immersive Halloween bar experience. The bar will be transformed into a Halloween-themed experience, with grandiose decor, black lighting, candles and seasonal cocktails.
  • The Pumpkin Patch at St. Andrew’s: is the largest pumpkin patch in New Orleans, where thousands of pumpkins of all sizes are available. The patch is open every day of the week and there is a children's maze available, as well as concessions.
  • Ghosts in the Oaks: A playful Halloween hangout inside City Park with arts and crafts, trick or treating, a pumpkin patch and campfires where attendees can roast s'mores and hot dogs. Carousel Gardens Amusement Park is also open and children are encouraged to dress up.
  • The Mortuary: A historic 1872 Victorian mansion that actually once housed a mortuary and is said to be home to nine ghosts. This year, the famous haunted house's theme is "Origins of Evil." It takes around 25 minutes to venture through The Mortuary and around 30,000 people visit the haunted house annually.
  • Cemetery at Night Tour with Nola Ghost Riders: This is the city's only after-dark cemetery tour and it showcases a few of New Orleans' 42 above-ground cemeteries. Historical guides are both entertaining and respectful and teach about unique burial rites and reported hauntings.
